title: Local integer normal forms on projective bundles
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E a quasi-coherent finite locally free module of constant rank r >= 2 [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and D any normalized tautological quotient on p:P(E)->S [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. For every invertible L on P(E) [def-sc-invertible-module] and s in S there are an open neighbourhood U of s and m in Z with L restricted to p^{-1}U isomorphic to D.line^{tensor m} restricted to p^{-1}U, using [def-pc-module-pullback] and [def-sfb-locally-constant-line-twist]. If S is isomorphic to Spec k for a field k, then for every invertible L there is a unique integer m with L isomorphic to D.line^{tensor m}. No coefficient descent or compatibility with tensor products is asserted.

source.place: Remark 4.2.7, printed p.75, local normal form; field calculation in Stacks divisors.tex Tag 0BXJ; coherent.tex Tag 07VK; limits.tex Tag 0B8W for arbitrary-base approximation.

proof.text: For a fixed invertible L and point s, the fibre-degree theorem gives an integer m and an isomorphism between the fibre restrictions of L and integerLinePower D.line m. The latter is invertible: nonnegative powers are tensor products of the line, and negative powers are tensor products of its dual. Apply fibre-isomorphism spreading to these two lines. Its neighbourhood and isomorphism give the local normal form.

source.place: Remark 4.2.7, fibre generator lifting and proper shrinking; Stacks coherent.tex Tag 07VK and limits.tex Tag 0B8W for arbitrary-base approximation.

proof.text: Over S isomorphic to Spec k, the base has a single point s. Apply the local clause there. Its neighbourhood equals the whole base. Pull the restriction isomorphism back along the inverse of the top-open scheme isomorphism, and use tensor-pullback identity and composition comparisons to obtain a global isomorphism L to the m-th power. For any competing degree n, pull both global isomorphisms to the fibre at s and apply uniqueness in the fibre-degree theorem. This gives n=m. The Lean proof uses explicit identity/composition comparisons, so it does not identify distinct restriction constructions definitionally.

proof_origin.place: Remark 4.2.7; the original four steps separated into fibre degree (Stacks 0BXJ) and isomorphism spreading (07VK, 0B8W), combined by top-open pullback and fibre uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem projective_bundle_local_normal_form (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (D : TautologicalQuotient E) :
    (∀ (L : (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProj.Modules),
      L.IsInvertible → ∀ s : S, ∃ U : S.Opens, s ∈ U ∧ ∃ m : ℤ,
        Nonempty ((tensorPullback
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).obj L ≅
          (tensorPullback
            ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).obj
            (integerLinePower D.line D.invertible m))) ∧
    (∀ (k : Type u) [Field k], (S ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) →
      ∀ L : (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProj.Modules,
        L.IsInvertible → ∃! m : ℤ, Nonempty (L ≅ integerLinePower D.line D.invertible m))
